subject: Foundation.dylib BridgeSupport re-export shim

observation.summary: scripts/bin/nm-symbols reports 46 global defined symbols in the Foundation.dylib BridgeSupport re-export shim, all of the form _NSMake*, _NSHeight/_NSWidth/_NSMinX/etc., _NSSwap*, _NSConvertHost*ToSwapped, _NSRange / _NSLocationInRange, _NSMakeCollectable, and the canonical toll-free helpers _CFBridgingRetain / _CFBridgingRelease (126 symbols in the dylib total). This shim is itself a small dyld-reexport stub that pulls in /System/Library/Frameworks/Foundation.framework/Versions/C/Foundation (compatibility version 300 / current version 5027.0.63) on macOS 27.
observation.raw_output_excerpt:
_CFBridgingRelease  T
_CFBridgingRetain   T
_NSDecimalIsNotANumber  T
_NSEdgeInsetsMake   T
_NSEqualRanges      T
_NSHeight           T
_NSLocationInRange  T
_NSMakeCollectable  T
_NSMakeRange        T
_NSMakeRect         T
_NSMakePoint        T
_NSMakeSize         T
_NSRange / _NSSwapBig* / _NSSwapLittle* / _NSConvertHost*ToSwapped  (full NSSwap family exported as global T symbols)

claim: On macOS 27 the canonical Foundation framework ships a BridgeSupport re-export dylib (Foundation.dylib, 120 KB, sha256 cf8c8657…) that exports the C-callable _NS* helper family plus the toll-free bridge helpers _CFBridgingRetain / _CFBridgingRelease — these are the only Mach-O-exported symbols for the Foundation framework that are actually on disk; the full ObjC class implementations live in the dyld shared cache.

cross_reference.label: Apple Foundation source mirror (closes the gap between the on-disk dylib and the runtime classes)
